title: Peer Memory (Person + Department)
markdown:
An external, peer-keyed memory layer gives the Executive durable cross-channel recall, sitting on top of Honcho via `openexecutive.memory.honcho_client`. The `HONCHO_ENABLED` env var gates it; when false every entry point short-circuits with `outcome=disabled` and behavior matches the pre-Honcho posture.

### Two scopes

- **Per-person**, keyed by `Person.id` — a user chatting from Discord, Telegram, email, or web is one peer card, so facts shared in any channel surface in the others. Each entry point resolves the caller to a `Person.id` (channel-ID lookups for adapters; `x-caller-email` for web).
- **Per-department**, keyed by `department_<slug>` — each department accumulates an institutional voice from dept-scoped decisions, advice, committee outcomes, and dept-bound specialist turns.

### Flow

`prefetch` runs once per turn, calling Honcho's dialectic endpoint and injecting a `<peer_memory>` block into the user turn (bounded by `HONCHO_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S`; empty on timeout). `prefetch_department` does the same per consulted specialist that maps to a department, yielding `<department_memory>`. After the response, `sync_turn` and `sync_department_turn` persist the exchange as fire-and-forget background tasks that never block the user.

### Cross-pollination & isolation

When a person turn touches a department, the dept peer joins the person's session as a co-present peer — the hybrid peer graph that lets later queries synthesize across both timelines, with synthesis depth degrading at greater peer-graph distance. Demo fixtures run in a sacrificial `openexec-fixture-<name>` workspace so demo turns never pollute real peer cards. Every wrapper call emits a `peer_memory` audit row (`op` + `outcome`) into the per-turn flow at `/audit/session/{id}`.
